name: IPhO
notes: ["The oldest and best known of the physics olympiads, first held in Warsaw in 1967. Each country sends up to five students for a theoretical and an experimental exam. Many older exams contain errors, catalogued in Stefan Ivanov's errata list .", "Files collected from IPhO Website ."]

name: EuPhO
notes: ["First held in Tartu in 2017, and deliberately unlike IPhO: problems are set to be solvable in elegant ways rather than long ones. Theory is three problems in five hours, with a separate experimental exam.", "Files collected from EuPhO Website ."]

name: APhO
notes: ["The Asian regional olympiad, first held in Indonesia in 2000. Teams are eight students rather than the five IPhO allows, and the exams are widely considered harder than IPhO's.", "Files collected from APhO Website . Experimental exams collected via phoXiv."]

name: NBPhO
notes: ["Began in 2003 as an Estonian and Finnish competition, joined by Latvia in 2014 and Sweden in 2016, when it took its present name. Around twenty students per country sit a single exam.", "Files collected from NBPhO Website ."]

name: OIbF
notes: ["First held in Bogotá in 1991, then lapsed for six years and resumed in Mexico in 1997. Teams of up to four sit a theoretical and an experimental exam, in Spanish and Portuguese.", "Files collected from OIbF Website .", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: RMPh
notes: ["An invitational olympiad in Bucharest, which began in 2010 as the physics side of the Romanian Master of Mathematics and Sciences and has been run on its own since 2015. Theoretical and experimental rounds.", "Files collected from RMPh Website ."]

name: WoPhO
notes: ["Ran only three times, from 2011. The format was unusual: a months-long open selection round anyone could enter, then a discussion round, then a final on site, with 142 students from 15 countries at the first. The 2013 final never took place.", "Files collected from WoPhO Website and the deepest parts of the Internet. The last three questions from 2011 and 2012 are from the final round of WoPhO, all the other problems are from the selection rounds. In 2013, the last year of the competition, only the selection round occurred."]

name: GPhO
notes: ["The Gulf regional olympiad, first held in Riyadh in 2016 and organised by ABEGS for the Gulf states. Three theory problems in five hours, plus a separate experimental exam.", "Files collected from GPhO Website . Organised by the Arab Bureau of Education for the Gulf States . Problems by Jaan Kalda, solutions by Taavet Kalda. Held in 2016, 2017, 2019 and 2022 only."]

name: IZhO
notes: ["A multi-subject olympiad held every January in Almaty, with a theory and an experimental paper in physics.", "Files collected from IZhO Website and phoXiv."]

name: ISPhO
notes: ["An international olympiad run since 2023 by MIPT near Moscow, built around problems drawn from current research, with theoretical and experimental rounds.", "Files collected from ISPhO Website and phoXiv."]

name: USAPhO
notes: ["The United States selection, run by AAPT since 1986. Thousands sit the F=ma exam; around 400 go on to the USAPhO, six problems in three hours, and twenty are picked for the team. Every sitting AAPT publishes is here, from F=ma to the training camp.", "Files collected from USAPhO Website . The Semifinal and USAPhO papers and solutions for 2008 to 2024 are the corrected 2026 edition by Kevin Zhou , former US Physics Team coach, who revised them for AAPT. F=ma answer keys rather than worked solutions for 2008 to 2012 and 2017.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: USA TST
notes: ["The last round of selection for the US IPhO team, sat at the Physics Team camp in Maryland; only a few years have been made public.", "Files collected from USA TST Website and phoXiv."]

name: CPhO
notes: ["The final round of the Chinese national olympiad, from which the IPhO team is chosen. The English translations are by Evan Liao.", "Files collected from CPhO Website and phoXiv. The English translations of the papers and solutions are by Evan Liao."]

name: PanPhO
full_name: Pan Pearl River Delta & Chinese Elite Schools Physics Olympiad
notes: ["Run by HKUST since 2005 for secondary schools across the Pan Pearl River Delta, and sat simultaneously in Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Macau. Papers are bilingual in English and Chinese, and divided into a part of shorter problems and a part of two or three long ones.", "Files collected from PanPhO Website . Papers up to 2017 come from the HKPhO archive .", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: VsOSh
notes: ["The final stage of the Russian national olympiad, the last of four rounds that begin in individual schools. Around 300 students reach it. Archived here is the grade 11 theoretical round; a practical round is also sat.", "Files collected from VsOSh Website . Final stage, grade 11, theoretical round. Papers are in Russian.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: Russia TST
notes: ["The selection of the Russian IPhO team, run in two stages, X and Y, each with theory, experimental and data-analysis problems; W is a preparatory round for 10th graders. Papers are in Russian.", "Files collected from Russia TST Website and phoXiv."]

name: MOSh
notes: ["First held in 1939, when 216 students entered and 28 reached the final, making it one of the oldest school physics competitions in Russia. Archived here is the final stage for grade 11, which is sat over two rounds.", "Files collected from MOSh Website . Final stage, grade 11, both written tours. Papers are in Russian.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: InPhO
notes: ["The second of five stages in the Indian selection, running since 1998. Some 300 to 400 students reach it out of the more than 40,000 who sit the NSEP screening exam below it.", "Files collected from InPhO Website . The detailed solutions for 2011 and 2012 are by Ashmit Dutta, via phoXiv.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: OBF
notes: ["First run nationally by the Brazilian Physics Society in 1999, when more than 13,000 students entered across 18 states. Archived here is the third phase, theoretical, Nível III, the last of three stages.", "Files collected from OBF Website . Papers are in Portuguese. Gabaritos exist for 2006 and 2007 only.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: SOIF
full_name: Seletiva das Olimpiadas Internacionais de Fisica
notes: ["The selection that picks Brazil's IPhO team from the top finishers of the Brazilian Physics Olympiad. Archived here is the first selection round; a second round and an experimental round are also sat.", "Files collected from SOIF Website . First selection round. Papers are in Portuguese, with official gabaritos."]

name: BPhO
notes: ["The UK's olympiad for sixth-formers: Round 1, sat in school in November, and Round 2, the invitation-only paper from which the IPhO team is chosen.", "Files collected from BPhO Website and phoXiv."]

name: ONF
notes: ["The national stage of the Romanian olympiad, the last of three rounds that begin at school and county level. Archived here is the grade 12 theoretical exam; a practical exam is also sat.", "Files collected from ONF Website . National stage, class XII, theoretical paper. Papers are in Romanian.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: UPhO
notes: ["Ukraine's national olympiad, held each spring with theoretical and experimental rounds for every grade; here is the 11th-grade theory paper.", "Files collected from UPhO Website and phoXiv."]

name: Eötvös
notes: ["One of the oldest physics competitions anywhere, first held in the autumn of 1916. It was started because the Eötvös Competition of 1894 had become purely mathematical. That first year was won by György Jendrassik, with Leó Szilárd second and Eugene Wigner commended.", "Files collected from Eötvös Website . Papers are in Hungarian. Official solutions are not published alongside the papers: they appear in each year's competition report (KöMaL, Fizikai Szemle), linked from the ELFT archive .", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: Fyziklani
notes: ["FYKOS's in-person team competition in Prague, held since 2006. Teams of up to five get three hours, starting with seven problems and unlocking harder ones as they solve them.", "Files collected from Fyziklani Website . Booklets before 2018 are in Czech. Published by FYKOS under CC BY-SA 3.0 .", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: EFO
notes: ["The final round of the Estonian olympiad, reached through a regional round. Archived here is the gymnasium level, in Estonian. The exams are also published in Russian, and a lower age group sits its own version.", "Files collected from EFO Website . Final round, gymnasium level. Papers are in Estonian.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: TwPhO TST
notes: ["Taiwan's selection for the IPhO team, run in two written rounds. Around 3,500 students sit the first; some 300 go through to the second, from which about 30 are chosen. Archived here is the second round.", "Files collected from TwPhO TST Website . Second selection round. Papers are in Chinese, with official marking schemes.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: TwPhO Camp
notes: ["The last round of Taiwan's IPhO selection, sat by about thirty students at a training camp: two written exams and a mock APhO. Papers are in Chinese.", "Files collected from TwPhO Camp Website and phoXiv."]

name: SPhO
notes: ["The first round of Singapore's selection for the IPhO, sat as written papers in the schools.", "Files collected from SPhO Website and phoXiv."]

name: SPhO TST
notes: ["The test from which Singapore picks its IPhO and APhO teams, one long written paper sat after the SPhO.", "Files collected from SPhO TST Website and phoXiv."]

name: SJPO
notes: ["An algebra-based olympiad for Singapore's secondary schools; the papers here are its general round, fifty multiple-choice questions in two hours.", "Files collected from SJPO Website and phoXiv. The 2022 and 2024 solutions are by PD Stem Education."]

name: KPhC
notes: ["A Korean competition for middle-school students aiming at the science high schools: thirty multiple-choice questions, in Korean.", "Files collected from KPhC Website and phoXiv."]

name: AuPhO
notes: ["The first round of Australia's selection for the IPhO, a written paper sat in schools and run by Australian Science Innovations.", "Files collected from AuPhO Website and phoXiv."]

name: OSN Fisika
notes: ["The Indonesian national science olympiad, which has included physics since its first edition in Yogyakarta in 2002. Archived here is the district round, the first of four, sat as a written test.", "Files collected from OSN Fisika Website . District stage (OSN-K; KSN-K in 2020 and 2021, when the competition was renamed Kompetisi Sains Nasional). Papers are in Indonesian.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: AzPhO
notes: ["The Azerbaijani physics olympiad, run by the education ministry's research institute. Archived here is the semi-final round at senior level. No official solutions are published.", "Files collected from AzPhO Website . Semi-final round, senior level. No official solutions are published.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: OPhO
notes: ["An online olympiad open to anyone, first run in May 2020. Teams of up to three enter an Open contest of numerical problems, and the strongest go through to an Invitational round marked from written solutions.", "Files collected from OPhO Website .", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: Physics Brawl
notes: ["An online team competition run by FYKOS from 2012, at its peak drawing 1,574 teams from 81 countries. Teams of five had three hours, starting with seven problems and unlocking more as they solved. The organisers ended it in 2025, citing the use of AI.", "Files collected from Physics Brawl Website . Published by FYKOS under CC BY-SA 3.0 ."]

name: Ortvay
notes: ["First run in 1970 and open internationally since 1998. It is not a sitting: the problems are published and contestants have about ten days to work at home, submitting at most ten of the thirty-odd offered. No official solutions are published.", "Files collected from Ortvay Website .", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: Physics Cup
notes: ["Jaan Kalda's competition, first run as a warm-up for IPhO 2012 and annual since 2017. One problem is released a month, and each week that passes without a solution publishes a further hint and lowers what the problem is worth.", "Files collected from Physics Cup Website . Later editions publish problems as web pages rather than PDFs.", "Titles marked * are ours, for problems the exam left unnamed."]

name: BAUPC
notes: ["A competition for undergraduates in the Boston area, run from 1995 to 2004, known for short, tricky problems; many reappear in Morin's Introduction to Classical Mechanics.", "Files collected from BAUPC Website and phoXiv."]
